transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Avery Collins (Redwood CSM); Michael Chen (LumenHealth Procurement), Laura Simmons (LumenHealth Legal), Ravi Patel (CTO), Sofia Lopez (InfoSec), Dana Ortiz (Finance), Ethan Moore (Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick procurement review; some audio glitch at start; multiple people joined from LumenHealth; recorded on Zoom.

00:00 Jordan Miles: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me?
00:05 Michael Chen: yeah loud and clear, thanks jordan.
01:12 Jordan Miles: quick agenda - we'll run through the redline, hit the DPA points, SLA ask, then pricing and onboarding. priya will cover perf and slas, and i will follow up on commercial and contract.
02:05 Priya Anand: hi all, priya here, i'll try to keep it high level then go into a couple of benchmark points, we did a small run against a 1k qps baseline then scaled to dedicated pods, so we'll share the spreadsheet.
03:18 Laura Simmons: just FYI legal side i'm primarily going to focus on indemnity, liability cap, and data processing terms. we need to understand how your private option handles data at rest and key management.
04:30 Sofia Lopez: and security - we need KMS/HSM integration specifics, key rotation, audit logs, and also SOC2 scope. also are there egress logs?
05:00 Jordan Miles: absolutely, we have SOC2 Type II, we can send the report. for KMS we support both cloud KMS and bring-your-own HSM for Private deployments, and for hosted we offer customer-managed keys for an extra control.
06:05 Ethan Moore: is that through a KMS connector or do you mount an HSM? how does onboarding work if we go private?
06:35 Priya Anand: for private we do a customer-controlled KMS via a connector + optional HSM. onboarding involves infra checklist - vpc peering or private link, firewall rules, and cert exchange. we'll send the onboarding runbook.
07:40 Dana Ortiz: on pricing - we need to lock committed spend and what happens if usage exceeds commit. also invoice cadence and PO requirements.
08:12 Jordan Miles: our Dedicated product is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commit. overage rates apply; we can put burst policies in place. we'll provide pricing tiers and a sample contract clause for overage billing.
09:20 Michael Chen: legal will want to see the MSA+DPA redline in docx so they can markup. pdfs are slow.
09:45 Jordan Miles: noted, we'll send editable redline.
10:10 Priya Anand: quick perf note - p95 latency in our hosted API for the model you asked about was ~110ms in our small benchmark but that's with optimistic batching; for predictable low-latency we'd recommend Dedicated with smaller batch windows, and we have guidance on quantization profiles.
11:30 Ravi Patel: when you say 110ms is that token latency or end-to-end completion? we've got real-time chat constraints.
12:00 Priya Anand: that was token latency measured client-side; end-to-end for a 256-token response was around 450ms in the test. for real-time chat we usually tune to P50 ~80-120ms token and p95 under 350 for dedicated.
13:20 Sofia Lopez: and what about KV cache - where's state stored? if a customer wants no prefix caching on hosted is that possible?
14:00 Priya Anand: yes we can disable persistent prefix caching; for Dedicated and Private you control the KV cache retention. hosted has TTL defaults but we can configure per-customer policies.
15:12 Laura Simmons: circling back on indemnity - your standard has broad language, we need a mutual indemnity clause and lower liability cap tied to fees. can you accept a liability cap of 1x ARR?
16:05 Jordan Miles: we can discuss; our standard is typically 2x annual fees for enterprise. we are open to negotiation for strategic customers, would need legal sign-off.
17:30 Laura Simmons: also data residency - we have EU patient data, so DPA must guarantee data at rest in EU region and deletion policy within 30 days after contract termination.
18:12 Jordan Miles: we support region pinning for private and dedicated, and hosted can be region-restricted. deletion policy we can hold to 30 days for retained logs; will confirm with engineering.
19:40 Sofia Lopez: audit logs - can we get per-token level logging off by default? we want redaction and PII masking.
20:10 Priya Anand: we recommend event-level logging with PII redaction; we have tooling to mask prompts in logs and an option for no persistent logs on private deployments.
21:00 Michael Chen: on SSO - we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning. need user and role sync, and RBAC mapping.
21:25 Jordan Miles: we support SAML SSO and SCIM, RBAC mapping in the console, and audit trails for admin actions.
22:40 Dana Ortiz: pricing again - can you provide an example invoice and the PO flow? we need billing entity name and tax details to start procurement.
23:12 Jordan Miles: yes, we'll include sample invoice and legal billing entity. also note we have both usage-based and committed pricing models; finance often prefers committed for predictability.
24:50 Laura Simmons: about the DPA, a couple of clauses are missing around subprocessors and 3rd party evals; we need a list of subprocessors and a right to audit clause.
25:30 Jordan Miles: we'll provide subprocessors list and a SOC2 attestation; right to audit can be discussed - many customers accept cert-based attestation rather than deep audits.
26:50 Priya Anand: on the SLA front - we propose 99.9% uptime for Hosted and SLA-backed targets for Dedicated. for latency SLOs we publish median and p95 numbers per model and we can put SLOs into contract with credits on miss.
28:10 Sofia Lopez: credits are fine but we want a clear remediation path and runbook for incidents, plus RTO/RPO expectations if Private.
29:00 Priya Anand: agreed, we'll attach an incident runbook and DR expectations for Private deployments.
30:15 Michael Chen: timeline - procurement wants to sign by end of month, legal needs two weeks to review redline. is that realistic?
31:00 Jordan Miles: yes, if we turn around the redline within 48 hours and priya provides the SLA deck within the week, that timeline looks possible.
32:25 Laura Simmons: one more on liability carveouts - we will push for exclusion for punitive damages and a cap tied to fees.
33:00 Jordan Miles: understood. we'll flag that item for legal.
34:10 Priya Anand: technical note - if you plan to do on-prem/private we have a deployment checklist that includes hostnames, firewall rules, cert exchange, and storage encryption guidelines. we'll share the runbook link in follow-up.
35:40 Ethan Moore: do you support air-gapped installs? we have a couple clients that require it.
36:05 Priya Anand: we have an optional on-prem package; air-gapped installs are supported but require professional services and longer lead time.
37:20 Michael Chen: ok, next steps for us - legal review, security checklist, pricing review with finance, then pilot decision.
38:00 Jordan Miles: to recap: jordan will send the docx redline, priya will send SLA/perf deck and onboarding runbook, we'll include subprocessors and SOC2, and finance will get sample invoice.
39:12 Laura Simmons: good, please include version history in the redline and highlight any non-standard clauses.
40:00 Jordan Miles: will do. any other questions?
41:10 Sofia Lopez: one small ask - can you provide KMS integration diagram and where keys are stored in hosted vs dedicated?
41:45 Priya Anand: yes, we'll include diagrams and an architecture note.
43:00 Dana Ortiz: i'll need net-30 invoice terms on the sample, or net-45 if we agree to certain conditions.
43:30 Jordan Miles: we'll include net-30 as standard and note options for net-45 on request.
44:20 Michael Chen: thanks everyone, we'll aim to get legal comments back by 4/21.
44:40 Jordan Miles: appreciate the time, we'll follow up with the artifacts within 48 hours.
45:00 Meeting closed.
